one_difference: cas/collision.rs::validate_candidates returns early when no foreign save holds a pack. Guard: SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM saves WHERE save_id != ?1 AND publication IS NOT NULL AND pack_ceiling > 0). Nothing else changes.
rationale: Squad B row 3 is SELECT ... WHERE o.object_id IN (?) AND o.pack_id <= ?2 at 25,245 calls, 7,083 ns/call, 178.8 ms - the third-largest statement on the row. It runs once per row inside validate_candidates, and its own next line discards every candidate that belongs to this save. On a store whose only prior content is this operation's own, every one of those lookups is therefore spent to prove nothing. The guard replaces 25,245 lookups with one two-row EXISTS per seal (16,595 of them).
why_it_is_exact_and_not_a_cache: The guard reads only published foreign saves, which is exactly the set the per-row lookup could return as a foreign candidate - the read scope is save_id = ours OR publication <= ours. It runs after begin_write, so this operation holds the store's write transaction and no foreign save can publish underneath it. A foreign save still preparing has publication IS NULL and is outside the read scope, so excluding it is correct rather than optimistic. pack_ceiling > 0 is equivalent to holding at least one object, because write_pack raises it on every pack a save creates.
not_changed: no capacity, policy constant or PRAGMA

expected_movement.pipeline.profile_sql_ns: 796,535,871 -> ~620-700 ms (Squad B's 178.8 ms for that statement, less ~17 ms of guard queries)
expected_movement.store file hash: UNCHANGED is expected here and is the strongest available check, because this treatment removes queries and stores nothing differently
